text_blocks.snippet: Common Scam Types in Central Illinois

list.snippet: Bank Impersonation & Phone Scams: Community banks—including Fisher National Bank and Federated Bank—have issued urgent warnings about spoofed phone calls that display real bank names or numbers to trick residents into sharing login credentials or financial data.

AI Voice & Romance Scams: Law enforcement in areas like Peoria County report a rise in AI-generated voice scams and romance scams, where fraudsters build online relationships over weeks before demanding money.

Tollway, Traffic Ticket & DMV Smishing: Phishing and smishing text messages falsely claim recipients owe money for unpaid tolls, traffic tickets, or vehicle registrations under threat of losing their driver's license. Official state portals like CyberDriveIllinois do not send text demands for payment.

State Agency & Court Impersonation: Scammers are impersonating Illinois state departments and federal/court officials (such as fake Central Violations Bureau or FBI/court investigator calls threatening sex-trafficking investigations or fines).
Door-to-Door Utility & Vacation Scams: Posing as energy suppliers (like Homefield Energy) or pushing fake vacation rentals and vague travel packages designed to harvest cash or data.
Hang up and call back: If you receive a call from your bank, court, or government agency, hang up and dial the official phone number listed on their verified website or mobile app.
Never click text links: Do not click links or call numbers provided in unsolicited text messages or emails regarding tolls, tickets, or account alerts.
Practice the pause: Scammers rely on manufactured urgency and secrecy; slow down and verify claims independently before sending any funds.
Report suspicious activity: Report text smishing and scams to the Federal Trade Commission or the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center.
